records.question: Which accounting jobs can software do, and which still need a person?
records.answer: Of the 16 accounting jobs in the library's map, software working from reliable event records can do 6 strongly: identity; authority; settlement; internal control; reconciliation; correction and recovery. Three more are strong once a condition holds: classification, when facts are complete; allocation, for fixed rules; reporting and disclosure, after judgments. Six can be done only partly: entity and perimeter; occurrence / existence; rights and obligations; recognition; close and consolidation; assurance. Measurement is mixed. The map's rule of thumb: the closer a function is to identity, authorization, arithmetic, sequencing and reconciliation, the more programmable it is. The closer it is to economic substance, legal rights, uncertain measurement and materiality, the more judgment remains.

records.question: How are big banks limiting group lawsuits in their customer contracts?
records.answer: Through their customer agreements: across 12 dated records from November 2018 to June 4, 2026, the library documents 8 banks and card issuers (Bank of America, Bread / Comenity, Chase, Citi, Cross River, PNC, Synchrony, Truist) using individual arbitration, waivers of class and group claims, and short mailed opt-out windows, and 3 records add special rules for mass filings. Each card links the contract or notice it comes from.

records.question: Which private shared-ledger settlement networks settle in central-bank money?
records.answer: Of the 12 market-infrastructure systems in the library, 1 is recorded as settling in central-bank money: the Sterling Fnality Payment System, run by Fnality UK Ltd (supervised by the Bank of England). 4 move banks' own tokenized deposits, which are commercial-bank money, and for the other 7 the library does not say what money they settle in.

records.question: Who really owns your loan?
records.answer: Often not the bank or brand you see. In Affirm's program agreements filed with the SEC (November 2020), Cross River Bank is the named lender, Affirm buys most of the loans, owns the customer information and services them, and Upstart processes applications and keeps the register of who owns the note. On the library's July 11, 2026 reading, the Affirm Card is issued by Evolve or Stride, not Cross River, and Upstart's note permits sale without borrower consent and discloses the owner only on written request.

records.question: Has the federal government really stopped sending paper checks?
records.answer: Mostly, not entirely. Executive Order 14247 (signed March 25, 2025 · published March 28, 2025) ordered an end to paper checks for federal payments, and a customs notice of July 8, 2026 says the government no longer sends them; but the Treasury's own April 29, 2026 proposal still sets out when agencies may send one, and the PBGC was moving its remaining paper-check recipients on June 24, 2026. In FY2026 Treasury screened >1.1 billion payment requests (about $3.7 trillion) before the money went out.

records.question: Did the ban on 'reputation risk' debanking become law, and at which agencies?
records.answer: It became agency regulation, not a law passed by Congress: the OCC and FDIC adopted a final rule (April 10, 2026); the NCUA adopted a final rule (June 25, 2026); the Federal Reserve Board has only proposed one (February 26, 2026). The NCUA's rule says it implements Executive Order 14331 (signed August 7, 2025 · published August 12, 2025).

records.question: What changes in your card or bank contract when your bank is sold?
records.answer: The library follows 6 bank sales and card-program moves since April 1, 2025 (Ally / Merrick, Capital One / Discover, Goldman, Fifth Third, Bilt / Column, PNC). In each, the brand, card number or app stays while the legal bank behind it changes, and the customer's new terms arrive on a separate, later clock; 2 conversions (Fifth Third, Goldman) have no customer contract published yet.

records.question: Which big banks have live tokenized deposits or deposit tokens?
records.answer: 4 of the 16 big institutions in the library have tokenized deposits or deposit tokens in use: J.P. Morgan, Citi, BNY and HSBC. The rest are piloting, have announced plans, or show nothing yet. 3 of the 16 are asset managers, not banks.

records.question: What has each card network and payment company actually launched with stablecoins?
records.answer: Of 32 stablecoin products from card networks and payment companies, 11 are fully live and 10 are live on a limited basis. 5 are pilots and 2 are announced only. In most live products the customer spends stablecoins while the shop is paid in ordinary money.

records.question: Where does the CLARITY market-structure bill stand, draft by draft?
records.answer: It is not law. The CLARITY Act (H.R. 3633) passed the House, and Senate sponsors released three public drafts: EHF26654 (616 pages, July 22, 2026), EHF26718 (630 pages, September 10, 2026) and EHF26724 (635 pages, September 14, 2026). None was formally filed as an amendment. On September 15, 2026 the Senate voted 49 to 50 on taking the bill up, short of the 60 votes needed, and the library's web check on October 19, 2026 found no later step.

records.question: How far has each big bank gone, capability by capability, and where does the proof stop?
records.answer: 16 institutions across 7 capabilities, all 112 cells printed in words: 81 cells are live or live-limited, and in 17 cells the master and the bank comparison read the status differently (both shown). Open any cell for where the proof stops.

records.question: What kind of money does each system settle in?
records.answer: 30 systems and money instruments, side by side: 5 stablecoin, 10 commercial-bank deposit token, 3 central-bank unit, 1 off-ledger final settlement, 1 carries more than one kind, 10 kind of money not stated in the row. A stablecoin is a claim on its issuer, a deposit token is a claim on one bank, a central-bank unit is a claim on the central bank, and several ledgers only coordinate payments that finally settle somewhere else.
